turn.user_message: What does a doctor have to do?
turn.context: Prompt 2 of bm-pr-03. bed-management.md §7.4.3: doctors speak on the round, and the agent shows a predicted date and summary for each patient. Transcript 23 and 27: show a date to confirm or correct, never ask for one.

transcript.label: After transcript turn 31 · Processes, turn 4 (the record stops at 31)

text: On the round the doctor speaks as usual. Tojo writes it down and shows a likely date for each patient.
bullets: The doctor confirms the date or changes it. Checking a date is quick. Making one up a day early is not.
A changed date is fine. It is not a rule broken, it just goes into the next plan.
If the round gets longer, something is wrong, and we change it.
chat.invite: Next, we can see what happens when a doctor will not confirm.
chat.note: Ask a doctor to check a date, never to make one up.
prompts: What if a doctor will not confirm a date?
Where do planned admissions come from?
chat.pointer: Confirm a date, or change it and type the new one. Pick a patient to see where the date comes from.

blocks.title: Check a date, do not make one
blocks.deck: One round, six patients. Each card shows the likely date. The doctor confirms or changes it.

blocks.round_line: Tojo writes it down. The doctor only checks each date.

patients.basis: Knee patients here stay about 5 days
Usual stay 3 days after the procedure

blocks.rule: The clinical call stays with the treating doctor. A changed date is logged, not a rule broken.
blocks.caption: Example patients, to show the round. Your own patients show once read access is in.

sheets.title: Knee replacement
sheets.text: The date comes from your own past knee patients and this patient’s notes. The doctor only checks it.
sheets.entry: Is this how your knee patients go?

sheets.title: Gall bladder removal
sheets.text: A short, regular stay. These are the dates most often confirmed with one word.
sheets.entry: Which stays are most regular for you?

sheets.title: Chest infection
sheets.text: Medical stays move more. A date that is changed is still useful. It goes into the next plan.
sheets.entry: Which wards have the longest stays?

sheets.title: Angioplasty
sheets.text: Planned procedures give the steadiest dates. They are where the plan gets most of its beds.
sheets.entry: How many angioplasties in a usual week?

sheets.title: Hip fracture
sheets.text: If the walking check is not passed, the doctor changes the date. The bed plan moves with it.

sheets.title: Diabetes control
sheets.text: A late date still helps. The bed can be planned for an evening patient instead of left to chance.

blocks.label: Extra time on the round
blocks.sub: The round already happens. If it takes longer, that is a fault to fix, not a cost to accept.
